library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

```{r load-model}
mod <- suppressMessages(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("oncology_xenograft_simeoni_2004")))
```

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-03-2524>

Simeoni 2004 introduced the tumor growth inhibition (TGI) model that has since
become the standard preclinical xenograft model. Tumor weight $w$ (g) grows
exponentially at rate $\lambda_0$ until it reaches $\lambda_1 / \lambda_0$ and
then linearly at rate $\lambda_1$; a single smooth function with
$\Psi = 20$ joins the two regimes (Eq. D). The drug moves proliferating cells
$x_1$ into a chain of three damaged, non-proliferating stages
$x_2 \ldots x_4$ at the rate $k_2 \, c(t) \, x_1$, and damaged cells pass
through the chain to death at the first-order rate $k_1$ (Eq. E):

$$
\frac{dx_1}{dt} = \frac{\lambda_0 x_1}{\left[1 + \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{\lambda_1} w\right)^{\Psi}\right]^{1/\Psi}} - k_2 c(t) x_1, \qquad
w = x_1 + x_2 + x_3 + x_4 .
$$

In the model file `cycling_cells` is $x_1$, `damaged_cells1`-`damaged_cells3`
are $x_2$-$x_4$ and `tumor_vol` is $w$. The model carries no PK: the plasma
concentration `Cc` (ng/mL) is an input, supplied in the data or by a PK model
composed upstream, and so is the initial tumor weight `tumor_vol0` ($w_0$, g).
The shipped parameter values are the paclitaxel experiment 1 estimates of
Table 2.

# Population

Female athymic Hsd nude (nu/nu) mice, 5-6 weeks old and 20-22 g, carried
subcutaneous A2780 human ovarian carcinoma xenografts implanted as tumor
fragments in the left flank (Methods, p. 1094-1095). Paclitaxel 30 mg/kg was
given as IV bolus doses every 4 days for 3 doses to groups of 8 mice in each of
two experiments, against vehicle controls. Tumor weight was computed from
caliper measurements as $\text{length} \cdot \text{width}^2 / 2$ at a density
of 1 mg/mm^3, so 1 g of tumor corresponds to 1000 mm^3. The model was fitted by
weighted least squares (WinNonlin 3.1) to the group-mean tumor weights of the
control and treated arms of both experiments simultaneously, sharing $k_1$ and
$k_2$ and estimating $\lambda_0$, $\lambda_1$ and $w_0$ per experiment.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("oncology_xenograft_simeoni_2004")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Unperturbed growth, smooth switch | $\Psi = 20$ | Eq. D and text, p. 1095 |
| Perturbed growth and damage chain | n/a | Eq. E and Fig. 1, p. 1096 |
| `ldamageTransit` ($k_1$) | `log(0.968)` 1/day | Table 2, p. 1098 |
| `ldrugSlope` ($k_2$) | `log(6.29e-4)` mL/(ng*day) | Table 2, p. 1098 |
| `ltumorExpGrowth` ($\lambda_0$, experiment 1) | `log(0.273)` 1/day | Table 2, p. 1098 |
| `ltumorLinGrowth` ($\lambda_1$, experiment 1) | `log(0.814)` g/day | Table 2, p. 1098 |
| `tumor_vol0` ($w_0$, input) | 0.055 g (experiment 1) | Table 2, p. 1098 |
| `propSd_tumor_vol`, `addSd_tumor_vol` | 0.2, 30 g | not in the reference |
| Paclitaxel PK (input `Cc`) | $V_1$ = 0.81 L/kg, $k_{10}$ = 0.868, $k_{12}$ = 0.0060, $k_{21}$ = 0.0838 1/h | Results, p. 1098 |

# Drug input: closed-form two-compartment PK

Simeoni 2004 fitted the PK of each drug separately (WinNonlin model 7, a
two-compartment IV bolus model) and used the typical profile as the input
$c(t)$ of the TGI model. The helper below evaluates that profile in ng/mL for
any set of bolus times (doses in mg/kg, $V_1$ in L/kg, rate constants in 1/h,
time in days). It is evaluated on a 0.002-day grid, with an extra point just
before every dose so that linear interpolation does not smear the jump at the
dose, and handed to `rxSolve()` as the time-varying `Cc` column.

```{r pk-helper}
# Concentration (ng/mL) of a two-compartment IV bolus model; superposition over
# dose_times (days). dose: mg/kg; v1: L/kg; k10, k12, k21: 1/h.
cc_2cmt <- function(time, dose_times, dose, v1, k10, k12, k21) {
  k10 <- k10 * 24
  k12 <- k12 * 24
  k21 <- k21 * 24
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  alpha <- (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  beta <- k10 * k21 / alpha
  conc <- numeric(length(time))
  for (td in dose_times) {
    dt <- time - td
    on <- dt >= 0
    conc[on] <- conc[on] + dose / v1 * 1000 *
      ((alpha - k21) / (alpha - beta) * exp(-alpha * dt[on]) +
        (k21 - beta) / (alpha - beta) * exp(-beta * dt[on]))
  }
  conc
}

# Simulate one arm: typical tumor weight for initial weight w0 (g) under the
# bolus regimen dose_times (none for a vehicle control).
run_arm <- function(model, w0, dose_times, dose, pk, tend) {
  time <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, tend, by = 0.002), dose_times, dose_times - 1e-6)))
  conc <- if (length(dose_times) > 0) {
    do.call(cc_2cmt, c(list(time = time, dose_times = dose_times, dose = dose), pk))
  } else {
    numeric(length(time))
  }
  events <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = time, evid = 0L, Cc = conc, tumor_vol0 = w0)
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    model, events,
    covsInterpolation = "linear", returnType = "data.frame",
    rtol = 1e-8, atol = 1e-10
  )
  data.frame(time = sim$time, tumor_vol = sim$tumor_vol, cycling_cells = sim$cycling_cells, Cc = conc)
}

trapz <- function(x, y) sum(diff(x) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

pk_paclitaxel <- list(v1 = 0.81, k10 = 0.868, k12 = 0.0060, k21 = 0.0838)
```

# Figure 7: paclitaxel in two experiments

Experiment 1 uses the shipped values; experiment 2 overrides $\lambda_0$ and
$\lambda_1$ with its own Table 2 estimates, and each experiment uses its own
$w_0$ as `tumor_vol0`. The two experiments share $k_1$ and $k_2$.

Table 2's experiment 1 parameter set reproduces the Figure 7 curves labelled
*exp 1* only when the three doses start on **Day 13**, at a tumor weight of
about 2 g. The experiment 2 set reproduces the *exp 2* curves when dosing
starts on **Day 8**. The Methods text and the captions of Table 2 and Figure 7
state the opposite assignment: experiment 1 from Day 8 and experiment 2 from
Day 13. Two features of the figure fix the mapping. First, each control line's
late slope equals its own experiment's $\lambda_1$: the solid *exp 1* control
rises at about 0.81 g/day and the dashed *exp 2* control at about 0.66 g/day.
Second, the solid treated line plateaus at about 2 g, the tumor weight at
Day 13. This article therefore simulates the Day 13 start for experiment 1 and
the Day 8 start for experiment 2, and the comparison under the caption's
assignment is shown below for completeness.

```{r figure-7-simulate}
mod_exp1 <- mod
mod_exp2 <- suppressMessages(rxode2::ini(mod, ltumorExpGrowth = log(0.311), ltumorLinGrowth = log(0.656)))

arms <- list(
  "exp 1 control" = run_arm(mod_exp1, 0.055, numeric(0), 30, pk_paclitaxel, 35),
  "exp 1 treated" = run_arm(mod_exp1, 0.055, c(13, 17, 21), 30, pk_paclitaxel, 35),
  "exp 2 control" = run_arm(mod_exp2, 0.033, numeric(0), 30, pk_paclitaxel, 35),
  "exp 2 treated" = run_arm(mod_exp2, 0.033, c(8, 12, 16), 30, pk_paclitaxel, 35)
)
sim7 <- bind_rows(arms, .id = "arm")

# Points read by the maintainers from the fitted lines of Figure 7 (g; read to
# about +/- 0.2 g).
fig7 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,            ~time, ~published,
  "exp 1 control",  13,    1.9,
  "exp 1 control",  23,    9.8,
  "exp 1 control",  31,   16.2,
  "exp 1 treated",  17,    2.5,
  "exp 1 treated",  21,    2.3,
  "exp 1 treated",  31,    6.3,
  "exp 2 control",  17,    5.0,
  "exp 2 control",  24,    9.0,
  "exp 2 control",  35,   16.3,
  "exp 2 treated",  17,    0.6,
  "exp 2 treated",  35,    9.3
)
fig7$simulated <- mapply(
  function(a, t) approx(arms[[a]]$time, arms[[a]]$tumor_vol, t)$y,
  fig7$arm, fig7$time
)
fig7$pct_diff <- 100 * (fig7$simulated - fig7$published) / fig7$published

fig7 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = arm, "Day" = time, "Figure 7 (g)" = published,
    "Simulated (g)" = simulated, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Tumor weight read from Figure 7 vs simulated.")

stopifnot(
  # A wrong k2, start day or PK unit shifts the treated curves by far more.
  abs(median(fig7$pct_diff)) < 10,
  max(abs(fig7$pct_diff)) < 20
)
```

```{r figure-7-plot}
ggplot(sim7, aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = arm, linetype = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig7, aes(time, published), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 4, size = 2) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "solid", "dashed", "dashed")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since inoculation (days)", y = "Tumor weight (g)",
    colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    title = "Figure 7 - paclitaxel 30 mg/kg q4d x 3",
    caption = "Lines: simulation. Crosses: values read from the fitted lines of Simeoni 2004 Figure 7."
  )
```

Under the caption's assignment the treated arms do not match the figure: the
experiment 1 parameters dosed from Day 8 hold the tumor near 0.5 g until
Day 21, where the solid *exp 1 treated* line is at about 2.3 g, and the
experiment 2 parameters dosed from Day 13 plateau near 2.3 g on Day 17, where
the dashed *exp 2 treated* line is at about 0.6 g.

```{r figure-7-caption-mapping}
caption_exp1 <- run_arm(mod_exp1, 0.055, c(8, 12, 16), 30, pk_paclitaxel, 35)
caption_exp2 <- run_arm(mod_exp2, 0.033, c(13, 17, 21), 30, pk_paclitaxel, 35)
w_caption_exp1_d21 <- approx(caption_exp1$time, caption_exp1$tumor_vol, 21)$y
w_caption_exp2_d17 <- approx(caption_exp2$time, caption_exp2$tumor_vol, 17)$y
c(exp1_day21 = w_caption_exp1_d21, exp2_day17 = w_caption_exp2_d17)
stopifnot(
  abs(w_caption_exp1_d21 / 2.3 - 1) > 0.5,
  abs(w_caption_exp2_d17 / 0.6 - 1) > 0.5
)
```

## Paclitaxel exposure

The grid-interpolated input reproduces the analytic AUC of three doses,
$3 \cdot \text{Dose} / (V_1 k_{10})$, and the clearance $V_1 k_{10}$ matches
the approximately 0.7 L/h/kg stated on p. 1098.

```{r paclitaxel-exposure}
treated <- arms[["exp 1 treated"]]
auc_grid <- trapz(treated$time, treated$Cc)
auc_analytic <- 3 * 30 / (0.81 * 0.868 * 24) * 1000 # ng*day/mL
c(auc_grid = auc_grid, auc_analytic = auc_analytic, cl_L_per_h_per_kg = 0.81 * 0.868)
stopifnot(abs(auc_grid / auc_analytic - 1) < 0.001)
```

## Unperturbed growth: closed forms

In a control animal the model must grow as $w_0 e^{\lambda_0 t}$ while $w$ is
far below the switch weight $\lambda_1/\lambda_0$ (2.98 g for experiment 1) and
with slope $\lambda_1$ well above it.

```{r unperturbed-closed-form}
ctl <- arms[["exp 1 control"]]
early <- ctl[ctl$time <= 6, ]
rel_err_exp <- max(abs(early$tumor_vol / (0.055 * exp(0.273 * early$time)) - 1))
late <- ctl[ctl$time >= 25, ]
slope_late <- unname(coef(lm(tumor_vol ~ time, data = late))[2])
c(rel_err_exponential = rel_err_exp, slope_late = slope_late, lambda1 = 0.814)
stopifnot(
  rel_err_exp < 1e-5,
  abs(slope_late / 0.814 - 1) < 1e-4
)
```

# Figure 11: time efficacy index against AUC (Drug A)

For a treatment given during exponential growth, Eq. F predicts a tumor-growth
delay, the time efficacy index, of $\text{TEI} = k_2 \cdot AUC / \lambda_0$.
Simeoni 2004 tested this with Drug A, a Pharmacia candidate given at 60 mg/kg
IV from Day 9 as qd x 11, bid x 4 or tid x 1, measuring TEI at a tumor weight
of 4 g. The regression of TEI on cumulative AUC through the origin had a slope
of 0.0012 mL/ng, against the theoretical $k_2/\lambda_0$ = 0.0011 mL/ng
(Fig. 11, p. 1099-1100). The simulation below uses the Drug A estimates from
the fit to all four arms (Table 4, right-hand columns) and its PK
($V_1$ = 1.96 L/kg, $k_{10}$ = 1.56, $k_{12}$ = 0.552, $k_{21}$ = 0.233 1/h;
p. 1099).

```{r figure-11}
mod_drugA <- suppressMessages(rxode2::ini(
  mod,
  ldamageTransit = log(0.355), ldrugSlope = log(3.76e-4),
  ltumorExpGrowth = log(0.355), ltumorLinGrowth = log(0.366)
))
pk_drugA <- list(v1 = 1.96, k10 = 1.56, k12 = 0.552, k21 = 0.233)
regimens <- list(
  "qd x 11" = 9 + 0:10,
  "bid x 4" = 9 + (0:7) / 2,
  "tid x 1" = 9 + (0:2) / 3
)
# First time (days) after the last dose at which the tumor weight reaches w.
time_to_weight <- function(sim, after, w) {
  s <- sim[sim$time >= after, ]
  i <- which(s$tumor_vol >= w)[1]
  approx(s$tumor_vol[c(i - 1, i)], s$time[c(i - 1, i)], w)$y
}
t_control <- time_to_weight(run_arm(mod_drugA, 0.009, numeric(0), 60, pk_drugA, 60), 0, 4)
fig11 <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = names(regimens),
  auc = vapply(regimens, function(d) length(d) * 60 / (1.96 * 1.56 * 24) * 1000, numeric(1)),
  tei = vapply(
    regimens,
    function(d) time_to_weight(run_arm(mod_drugA, 0.009, d, 60, pk_drugA, 60), max(d), 4) - t_control,
    numeric(1)
  )
)
slope_sim <- sum(fig11$tei * fig11$auc) / sum(fig11$auc^2)
fig11 |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Cumulative AUC (ng*day/mL)" = auc, "TEI at 4 g (days)" = tei) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated TEI and cumulative AUC of Drug A.")
c(slope_simulated = slope_sim, slope_published = 0.0012, slope_theory = 3.76e-4 / 0.355)
stopifnot(
  abs(slope_sim / 0.0012 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(slope_sim / (3.76e-4 / 0.355) - 1) < 0.15
)
```

```{r figure-11-plot}
ggplot(fig11, aes(auc, tei, label = regimen)) +
  geom_abline(slope = slope_sim, intercept = 0) +
  geom_abline(slope = 0.0012, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(nudge_y = 0.6) +
  expand_limits(x = 0, y = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Cumulative AUC (ng*day/mL)", y = "TEI at 4 g (days)",
    title = "Figure 11 - Drug A",
    caption = "Solid: regression through the origin on the simulation. Dashed: published slope 0.0012 mL/ng."
  )
```

# Threshold concentration and Drug B infusion (Figure 13)

At a constant concentration $C_{ss}$ the tumor is eradicated if
$C_{ss} > C_T = \lambda_0 / k_2$; otherwise it settles at
$w_{ss} \approx \lambda_1 / (k_2 C_{ss})$ (p. 1096-1097). From the Drug B bolus
fit (Table 5: $\lambda_0$ = 0.309 1/day, $k_2$ = 2.89e-4 mL/(ng*day)) the
paper quotes $C_T$ of about 1100 ng/mL (p. 1099). Holding Drug B at half that
threshold, the simulated tumor weight converges to the exact steady state of
Eq. E, $w_{ss} = (\lambda_1/\lambda_0)\left[(\lambda_0/(k_2 C_{ss}))^{\Psi} - 1\right]^{1/\Psi}$,
which the paper's approximation matches to within $10^{-6}$.

```{r threshold-concentration}
lambda0_b <- 0.309
lambda1_b <- 0.796
k2_b <- 2.89e-4
ct_b <- lambda0_b / k2_b
mod_drugB <- suppressMessages(rxode2::ini(
  mod,
  ldamageTransit = log(0.517), ldrugSlope = log(k2_b),
  ltumorExpGrowth = log(lambda0_b), ltumorLinGrowth = log(lambda1_b)
))
css <- ct_b / 2
time_ss <- c(0, 9, seq(9.01, 300, by = 1))
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_drugB,
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = time_ss, evid = 0L, Cc = ifelse(time_ss > 9, css, 0), tumor_vol0 = 0.034),
  covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
)
w_ss_exact <- lambda1_b / lambda0_b * ((lambda0_b / (k2_b * css))^20 - 1)^(1 / 20)
w_ss_paper <- lambda1_b / (k2_b * css)
c(ct = ct_b, w_ss_simulated = tail(sim_ss$tumor_vol, 1), w_ss_exact = w_ss_exact, w_ss_paper = w_ss_paper)
stopifnot(
  abs(ct_b / 1100 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(tail(sim_ss$tumor_vol, 1) / w_ss_exact - 1) < 1e-6,
  abs(w_ss_paper / w_ss_exact - 1) < 1e-5
)
```

Simeoni 2004 then gave Drug B as a 7-day IV infusion from Day 9 targeting about
2000 ng/mL; the observed mean steady state was 2085 ng/mL, about twice $C_T$,
and the tumors started to shrink as predicted (Fig. 13). With the parameters
of the fit to the infusion experiment (Table 5, infusion column: $k_1$ =
0.615 1/day, $k_2$ = 2.93e-4 mL/(ng*day), $\lambda_0$ = 0.369 1/day,
$\lambda_1$ = 0.511 g/day, $w_0$ = 0.016 g) and the concentration held at
2085 ng/mL during the infusion, the proliferating population collapses and the
total tumor weight falls from its peak before regrowing after the infusion
stops. The rise of the concentration to steady state, with a half-life of
under an hour, is neglected.

```{r figure-13}
mod_drugB_inf <- suppressMessages(rxode2::ini(
  mod,
  ldamageTransit = log(0.615), ldrugSlope = log(2.93e-4),
  ltumorExpGrowth = log(0.369), ltumorLinGrowth = log(0.511)
))
time_inf <- sort(c(seq(0, 30, by = 0.05), 16 + 1e-6))
sim13 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_drugB_inf,
  data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = time_inf, evid = 0L,
    Cc = ifelse(time_inf > 9 & time_inf <= 16, 2085, 0), tumor_vol0 = 0.016
  ),
  covsInterpolation = "linear", returnType = "data.frame"
)
x1_day9 <- sim13$cycling_cells[sim13$time == 9]
x1_day16 <- sim13$cycling_cells[sim13$time == 16]
w_peak <- max(sim13$tumor_vol[sim13$time >= 9 & sim13$time <= 16])
w_day16 <- sim13$tumor_vol[sim13$time == 16]
c(ct_infusion_fit = 0.369 / 2.93e-4, x1_day9 = x1_day9, x1_day16 = x1_day16, w_peak = w_peak, w_day16 = w_day16)
stopifnot(
  2085 > 0.369 / 2.93e-4,
  x1_day16 < 0.25 * x1_day9,
  w_day16 < 0.8 * w_peak
)

sim13 |>
  select(time, "total (tumor_vol)" = tumor_vol, "proliferating (cycling_cells)" = cycling_cells) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = name)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 9, xmax = 16, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since inoculation (days)", y = "Tumor weight (g)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Figure 13 - Drug B 7-day infusion at 2085 ng/mL (shaded)"
  )
```

# Changing the number of damage stages

The paper uses three damage stages and notes that more stages make the
distribution of time to death more bell-shaped, with mean $n / k_1$ (Fig. 2).
`updateOncologyXenograftSimeoni2004()` rebuilds the chain with any number of
stages. Rebuilding with three stages must reproduce the shipped model.

```{r update-ncmt}
mod_3 <- suppressMessages(updateOncologyXenograftSimeoni2004(mod, ncmt = 3))
mod_5 <- suppressMessages(updateOncologyXenograftSimeoni2004(mod, ncmt = 5))
time_n <- seq(0, 30, by = 0.25)
ev_n <- data.frame(
  id = 1L, time = time_n, evid = 0L,
  Cc = ifelse(time_n >= 10 & time_n < 12, 5000, 0), tumor_vol0 = 0.055
)
sim_ref <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_n, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
sim_3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_3, ev_n, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
sim_5 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_5, ev_n, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
max_rel_diff_3 <- max(abs(sim_3$tumor_vol / sim_ref$tumor_vol - 1))
max_rel_diff_3
stopifnot(max_rel_diff_3 < 1e-6)

bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = time_n, tumor_vol = sim_ref$tumor_vol, stages = "3 (shipped)"),
  data.frame(time = time_n, tumor_vol = sim_5$tumor_vol, stages = "5")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = stages)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since inoculation (days)", y = "Tumor weight (g)", colour = "Damage stages",
    title = "Damaged cells take longer to die with more stages (mean n / k1)"
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Experiment labels in Figure 7.** The Methods (p. 1095) and the captions of
  Table 2 and Figure 7 put the first paclitaxel dose of experiment 1 on Day 8
  and of experiment 2 on Day 13. The Table 2 parameter sets reproduce the
  figure's fitted curves only with the opposite assignment, as shown above, so
  this article doses experiment 1 from Day 13 and experiment 2 from Day 8. The
  shipped values are the Table 2 experiment 1 column either way.
- **Paclitaxel peak concentration.** The printed PK ($V_1$ = 0.81 L/kg) gives
  a peak of 37 ug/mL after 30 mg/kg, whereas the text (p. 1098) quotes maximal
  concentrations of about 110 ug/mL. The printed $V_1$ is used because it
  matches the stated clearance of about 0.7 L/h/kg ($V_1 k_{10}$) and
  reproduces the treated curves of Figure 7; a three-fold smaller $V_1$ at the
  same $k_{10}$ would triple the AUC and the growth delay.
- **Initial tumor weight is an input.** Simeoni 2004 estimated $w_0$ with the
  other parameters; the model takes it from the data as `tumor_vol0`, and this
  article supplies the published estimates. The name keeps `vol` although the
  quantity is a weight in g; at the paper's density of 1 mg/mm^3, 1 g equals
  1000 mm^3.
- **Residual error.** Simeoni 2004 fitted group means by weighted least
  squares (uniform, 1/y or 1/y^2 weights chosen per data set) and reports no
  residual-error model. The shipped `propSd_tumor_vol = 0.2` and
  `addSd_tumor_vol = 30` are not from the paper; with tumor weight in g, an
  additive SD of 30 g exceeds every tumor weight in the paper, so simulate
  with residual error only after replacing it. All simulations here are
  typical-value predictions without residual error, and the model has no
  between-animal variability.
- **Parameter bounds.** The lower and upper bounds in `ini()` are not from the
  paper.
- **Other drugs.** Drug A (Table 4) and Drug B (Table 5) values are applied
  with `ini()` overrides for the secondary-parameter checks; the model file
